title: Review: Molar gas volume and Avogadro's law; Atom economy; Structural isomerism
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: OR04#t2 term and clue written for the game; OR04#t3 term and clue written for the game; AM10#t1 term and clue written for the game; AM10#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AM05#N.10a, AM10#N.3, OR04#N.8, AM05#N.7a, AM10#N.5, OR04#N.9, AM05#N.4, AM10#N.9, OR04#N.7, OR04#N.4. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Position isomers
items.clue: The same group at a different place, e.g. propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol.

items.label: Functional group isomers
items.clue: One molecular formula but different families, e.g. propanal and propanone.

items.label: Atom economy
items.clue: Percentage of the total mass of reactants that ends up in the desired product.

items.label: Addition reaction
items.clue: Gives a single product, so 100% of the starting mass ends up in what is wanted.

questions.stem: Two identical flasks at the same temperature and pressure are filled, one with neon, Ne, and one with sulfur hexafluoride, SF₆, a dense gas used in electrical switchgear. The SF₆ flask holds 7.2 times the mass of gas. Which statement is correct? (Ar: F 19.0, Ne 20.2, S 32.1)

options.text: The SF₆ flask holds 7.2 times as many particles as the neon flask.
The neon flask holds more particles, because neon atoms are much smaller.
Both flasks hold the same number of particles; each SF₆ molecule is about 7.2 times heavier.
Both flasks hold the same number of atoms, so there are 7 times as many Ne atoms as SF₆ molecules.

questions.explanation: Avogadro's law: same V, T and p → same number of particles. 146.1 ÷ 20.2 = 7.2.

questions.stem: Which statement about atom economy and waste in an industrial process is correct?

options.text: The higher the percentage yield, the higher the atom economy, so less waste is produced.
Atom economy counts one molecule of each substance, so the coefficients do not affect it.
A process with an atom economy of 100% produces no waste of any kind at all.
The lower the atom economy, the greater the proportion of reactant mass that becomes waste.

questions.explanation: The mass not in the desired product ends up in by-products, so atom economy and waste are inversely related.

questions.stem: Classify each halogenoalkane. P: (CH₃)₂CHCH₂Cl. Q: CH₃CHICH₃. R: 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane (Br and CH₃ on the same ring carbon). Which row is correct for P, Q and R?
questions.explanation: P: the CH₂Cl carbon is bonded to one carbon. Q: the CHI carbon to two. R: the C–Br carbon to two ring carbons and the CH₃: three.

questions.stem: Magnesium reacts with excess dilute hydrochloric acid: Mg(s) + 2HCl(aq) → MgCl₂(aq) + H₂(g). What volume of hydrogen, in cm³ at RTP, forms from 0.120 g of magnesium? (Ar: Mg 24.3; molar gas volume 24.0 dm³ mol⁻¹ at RTP)
Which reaction has an atom economy of 100% for the product named?

options.text: CaCO₃(s) → CaO(s) + CO₂(g), making calcium oxide
Any reaction that is carried out with a 100% yield

questions.explanation: This reaction has a single product, so every reactant atom ends up in it: 100%.

questions.stem: How many structural isomers, hexane included, have the molecular formula C₆H₁₄?
questions.explanation: Hexane; 2-methylpentane; 3-methylpentane; 2,2-dimethylbutane; 2,3-dimethylbutane. Every other drawing is one of these.

questions.stem: Sulfur dioxide reacts with oxygen: 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2SO₃(g). What volume of oxygen reacts completely with 30.0 cm³ of sulfur dioxide? All volumes are measured at the same temperature and pressure.
questions.explanation: Same T and p, so volumes are in the coefficient ratio: 30.0 × 1/2 = 15.0 cm³.

questions.stem: Hydrogen is manufactured by reacting methane with steam: CH₄(g) + H₂O(g) → CO(g) + 3H₂(g). In one batch, 16.0 kg of methane gave 4.80 kg of hydrogen. What is the atom economy for producing hydrogen by this reaction? (Aᵣ: H 1.0, C 12.0, O 16.0)
questions.explanation: 3 × 2.0 ÷ (16.0 + 18.0) × 100 = 6.0 ÷ 34.0 × 100 = 17.6%. The products total is the same: 28.0 + 6.0 = 34.0. The rest of the mass ends up as CO.

questions.stem: Which compound is a tertiary alcohol?
questions.explanation: The carbon carrying –OH is bonded to three carbons (two CH₃, one CH₂CH₃): 2-methylbutan-2-ol is tertiary.

questions.stem: Which pair of compounds are position isomers?
questions.explanation: Both are C₅H₁₂O alcohols on the same unbranched chain; only the –OH position differs (pentan-1-ol, pentan-3-ol).
